title: Build a Stage 7 Computing Showcase
overview: Bring together everything from Stage 7 Computing into one showcase: a working program, the data behind it, a clear explanation of how it runs, and the safety rules you followed while making it.

project.drivingQuestion: How can I use the computing I learned in Stage 7 to build something that solves a real problem for someone in my community — and explain exactly how it works?
project.finalProduct: A working program or digital product, the plan and algorithm behind it, a test-and-debug log, a data display, and a spoken or written explanation of your design decisions.

stages.title: 1. Plan and decompose
stages.prompt: Choose a real problem. Using the ideas from Units 1, 2, break it into smaller parts and write the algorithm before you write any code.
stages.evidence: A decomposed problem and a written algorithm or flowchart

stages.title: 2. Build it
stages.prompt: Build your program or product using the tools from Units 3, 4. Build the smallest working version first, then add one feature at a time.
stages.evidence: A working program or digital product

stages.title: 3. Test, debug and improve
stages.prompt: Test your work against your success criteria. Keep a log of every bug: what you saw, what caused it, and how you fixed it.
stages.evidence: A test-and-debug log with at least three entries

stages.title: 4. Share it safely
stages.prompt: Present your showcase. Explain three design decisions, show your data, and say which online-safety rules from Units 5, 6 you followed and why.
stages.evidence: A spoken, written or recorded explanation covering design, data and safety

evidenceChecklist: A decomposed problem with a written algorithm or flowchart
A working program or digital product
A test-and-debug log with at least three fixed bugs
Success criteria, each one ticked off with evidence
An explanation of your design decisions and the safety rules you followed

rubric.secure: The problem is decomposed, the algorithm is precise, and the pattern behind it is named.
The program runs, meets its criteria, and every bug found is logged with its cause and fix.
Data is collected accurately, organised sensibly and displayed so it answers a question.
Personal information is protected, sources are credited, and safety choices are explained.

questions.question: What does “text-based programming” mean in computing?
options: Programming where you type the code as text, using a language such as Python.
Programming by dragging and dropping blocks that snap together, as in Scratch.
A popular, free, text-based programming language. You will use it all through this unit.
A program that helps you write, save, test and run code. Thonny and IDLE are both Python IDEs.
questions.answer: Programming where you type the code as text, using a language such as Python.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Text-based programming means programming where you type the code as text, using a language such as Python..

questions.question: What does “Python shell” mean in computing?
options: Python's interactive mode, where you type one command and see the result straight away.
A way of using Python where each command is run immediately in the shell.
Python's editor, where you type a list of commands, save them as a file, and run them together.
A Python command that outputs text or values onto the screen.
questions.answer: Python's interactive mode, where you type one command and see the result straight away.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: IDE (Integrated Development Environment) means a program that helps you write, save, test and run code. Thonny and IDLE are both Python IDEs.

questions.question: What does “accelerometer” mean in computing?
options: A sensor that detects movement, tilt and gestures such as a shake.
A sequence of steps or instructions to solve a problem.
Following the flow of a flowchart with a specific input to predict the output.
Software for general or specific tasks, such as a browser or word processor.
questions.answer: A sensor that detects movement, tilt and gestures such as a shake.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 2 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Accelerometer means a sensor that detects movement, tilt and gestures such as a shake..

questions.question: What does “automate” mean in computing?
options: To let sensors and a program run a device with little or no human interaction.
A symbol used to compare values, such as >, <, >=, <=, ==, !=.
Any device that follows the input, process, output model.
The process of finding and removing errors from a program.
questions.answer: To let sensors and a program run a device with little or no human interaction.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 2 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Applications software means software for general or specific tasks, such as a browser or word processor.

questions.question: Which computing word matches this meaning: Another word for running a program.?

flashing the program
flowchart
gesture

questions.question: What does “connectivity” mean in computing?
options: The way devices connect to each other to form a network.
A group of computers and devices connected so they can share data.
The huge global network that connects billions of devices worldwide.
A wireless method of connecting devices using radio waves, over a short range.
questions.answer: The way devices connect to each other to form a network.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 3 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Connectivity means the way devices connect to each other to form a network.

options: A wireless method for connecting nearby devices using radio waves.
Mobile internet from phone masts, such as 4G and 5G.
The amount of data that can be sent in a certain amount of time.
How far a signal can travel using a transmission method.
questions.answer: A wireless method for connecting nearby devices using radio waves.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 3 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Bluetooth means a wireless method for connecting nearby devices using radio waves.

IP address
URL

questions.question: What does “data” mean in computing?
options: Raw facts and figures, for example a list of names or prices.
Examine something in detail so that you fully understand it.
A computer representation of a real-life situation, where data is changed to see what happens.
A more complex model that can predict the outcome of a real-world system, often using graphics.
questions.answer: Raw facts and figures, for example a list of names or prices.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 4 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Data means raw facts and figures, for example a list of names or prices.

questions.question: What does “factors” mean in computing?
options: The key data items represented in a data model.
An application that uses rows and columns to organise data and carry out calculations (LibreOffice Calc).
An application used to organise data so it can be stored, processed and accessed electronically (LibreOffice Base).
The box where a row and a column meet; it can hold text, a number or a formula.
questions.answer: The key data items represented in a data model.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 4 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Factors means the key data items represented in a data model.

function
relative reference

questions.question: What does “Software” mean in computing?
options: The programs and instructions that tell a device what to do. You cannot touch software.
The physical parts of a device that you can touch, such as the screen, keyboard and battery.
Software that runs and manages the device itself, for example the operating system.
The most important systems software; it manages the hardware and lets you use other programs.
questions.answer: The programs and instructions that tell a device what to do. You cannot touch software.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 5 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Software means the programs and instructions that tell a device what to do. You cannot touch software.

questions.question: What does “Application software” mean in computing?
options: Software that helps you do a task you want to do, such as a browser or a camera app.
Technology that lets a computer act or think in a way similar to a human.
A type of AI that learns and improves by finding patterns in large amounts of data.
To let a device complete a task on its own, with little or no human help.
questions.answer: Software that helps you do a task you want to do, such as a browser or a camera app.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 5 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Application software means software that helps you do a task you want to do, such as a browser or a camera app.

questions.question: What does a sequence mean in programming?
options: a random set of steps
the specific order of instructions
a type of loop
a picture on the display
questions.hint: Use the Unit 6 Computing Words reference.

questions.question: What is the value range for LED brightness?
options: 0 to 1
0 to 9
questions.hint: Use the Unit 6 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: 0 to 9. 0 is off, 9 is full brightness, and 1 to 8 are dimmer levels.
